trust_decision.summary: The trust decision is 'may this username/password/code tuple produce a session?', taken in core/user/service.go Authenticate and backed by a per-user 'was this TOTP code already used' compare-and-set on the user table; however at pinned 91976f0 nothing in the tree verifies a TOTP code at all (the feature, its handlers, its columns and its routes are added by fix commit 1cbfae0, whose parent is this pin), so the supplied pin sits before the feature and no flaw exists in it to fix.

landing_point.why: An engineer who read only 'TOTP Reuse During Validity Window' opens the login request path first; at the pinned commit it reads username/password only and calls Authenticate with no code argument (core/user/service.go:28).

fix_sites.entry_point: every user read/write through the repository (Save, FindByID)
every user read/write through the repository
POST /api/users/login via the core Repository port

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The replay history is a varchar column plus its converter in database/user, which can be written off as persistence plumbing the login check never calls, and the admin user-edit path (PUT /api/users/:id) can be written off as user management rather than login replay.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Logins that must keep working: a TOTP-disabled user, and the onboarding first login which calls Authenticate with no code, must still authenticate; and a second, different code from an adjacent time step is legitimately valid, which is why the fix keeps three codes rather than one - a fix that rejects any login inside the current window, or keeps only the last code, breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: login body with no "totp" field (nil pointer normalised to "")
empty totp string, including for a TOTP-disabled user
a code still present earlier in the three-code history
a code submitted to POST /api/users/current/totp/activate, where activation also validates a code
zero-padded numeric codes stored comma-joined in one 20-character column

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PUT /api/users/:id (admin user update) carrying a password: service.Save builds a fresh User and saves it, so the TOTP secret, the validated flag and the used-code history are all cleared; a code used before the update can be replayed afterwards and 2FA is silently disabled.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is an admin user-edit path, not the login endpoint the advisory names, and the advisory's example (a replayed code at login) still fails without touching it.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: one operation away from Authenticate in the same core/user service; 1 file / 1 package from the landing point, but the defect only appears once the feature commit's Save carries TOTP state

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second writer of user state (Save) that rebuilds User from the request instead of merging the stored one, so any new per-user security field is silently dropped.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already drops every field it does not explicitly copy; a maintainer adding a second one-time-secret feature (password-reset token, backup-code list) would extend the same pattern here.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A configuration-driven password reset that saves the loaded user, a plausible place for a second 'reset security state' path.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already resets credentials from configuration at startup, so a 'clear used codes when the admin resets a password' rule would naturally live on this path too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second caller of Authenticate outside the login handler, which would need the same code argument and the same replay handling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already authenticates from the onboarding flow, so a future 'authenticate after account creation' or re-authentication endpoint would be added beside it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The generic whole-row Save/upsert that converts and writes every column, a parallel writer to the targeted UPDATE in TryUpdateLastUsedTOTPCode.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every new user column must be carried through toModel/toDomain here; a maintainer adding used-code tracking could add only one of the two writers.

O9_family: improper authentication (CWE-287) - TOTP code replay across the validity window
